awards_draft#u1.description: Five live series are TITLE_ONLY (KXNBATOP3, KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBADRAFTTRADE, KXNBADRAFTCONF, KXNBADRAFTINT), so their construction is inferred; among texts that exist, All-NBA/All-Defensive/All-Rookie, MVP, DPOY, ROY and Sixth Man have no tie clause, and KXNBAALLSTARS does not say whether injury replacements count as 'selected'.
awards_draft#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample rules for the five TITLE_ONLY series and read Kalshi's rulebook on ties and replacement selections.

awards_draft#u2.description: Voter ballots are public only after announcement, and the electorate composition and any strategic voting (fatigue, ballot pre-commitment before the playoffs) cannot be observed during the season.
awards_draft#u2.what_would_resolve: Collect past ballot-level data and test whether voter-level fatigue and homers add information; accept residual uncertainty otherwise.

awards_draft#u3.description: Current 2026-27 eligibility details (20-minute definition, two 15-20 minute allowance) and positionless All-NBA ballot rules are from memory of the 2023 CBA and have not been re-read in the 2026-27 league rulebook. Which awards the rule governs (and that it does not govern monthly awards, Coach or Executive of the Year, All-Star selection or draft markets) is likewise unverified.
awards_draft#u3.what_would_resolve: Read the league's published award criteria for the 2026-27 season and confirm each threshold.

awards_draft#u4.description: Leak timing: reporters often release award or draft results hours before the official announcement, and it is unclear whether Kalshi settles on the leak or the official release.
awards_draft#u4.what_would_resolve: Compare settlement timestamps of past awards with leak times; confirm from rules_primary text.

awards_draft#u5.description: The All-Star formula weights (50/25/25), the five-starter and seven-reserve split by position group per conference, wildcard rules and the availability of historical early-return fan-vote snapshots are from memory of recent seasons and have not been checked against the 2027 rules or a machine-readable archive.
awards_draft#u5.what_would_resolve: Read the league's published All-Star selection rules for 2027 and check whether early-return snapshots exist in a machine-readable archive.

awards_draft#u6.description: The Hustle Award (KXNBAHUSTLE) is decided from tracked hustle statistics (deflections, charges, loose balls, screen assists, contests) and no input here aggregates them; the Teammate and Sportsmanship player votes are carried only by the generic nominee model, so these three remain thinly modelled.
awards_draft#u6.what_would_resolve: Create dedicated archetypes (Hall of Fame election, All-Star Weekend events, season stat leader) or confirm the existing season_stat_markets record defines stat-leader inputs.

awards_draft#u7.description: The draft-slot texts are silent on a rescheduled draft and on forfeited picks, and the award texts do not say whether league eligibility determinations bind settlement; KXNBADRAFTTEAM now states undrafted resolves No and post-selection trades are ignored.
awards_draft#u7.what_would_resolve: Sample rules_secondary for the draft-slot, monthly-award and Hall of Fame series and read any wording on trades, withdrawal and eligibility.

awards_draft#u8.description: The Hall of Fame procedure (finalists named at All-Star weekend, class announced in April, an honors-committee threshold recalled as 18 of 24 votes, direct-elect committees) and the selection procedures for the Social Justice, Teammate and Sportsmanship awards are recalled and were not re-read for the 2027 class.
awards_draft#u8.what_would_resolve: Read the Hall's current election rules and the league's 2026-27 award procedure releases.

combo_props#u1.description: The sampled KXNBAPRA and KXNBAPRAPROT texts do not say whether overtime statistics count toward the three-stat total, and the points+rebounds (KXNBAPR) and points+assists (KXNBAPA) series are TITLE_ONLY, so their DNP and OT wording is not visible.
combo_props#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample rules_primary for unprotected combo series when they list, and read any statement on overtime in the rule text.

combo_props#u2.description: Per-game tracking data for potential assists and rebound chances is paid or rate-limited and the per-game grain of the free endpoint was not verified.
combo_props#u2.what_would_resolve: Verify the nba_api tracking endpoint at game grain or price a Second Spectrum/Sportradar feed.

combo_props#u3.description: The regime split of minutes (blowout, foul, OT, restriction) uses thresholds chosen from basketball judgement; cutoffs like margin 18 or 4 fouls by Q3 are not validated and may be coach-specific.
combo_props#u3.what_would_resolve: Check the cutoffs against the empirical minute histograms per coach and relabel regimes from data.

combo_props#u4.description: Lineup-conditional rates need 300 possessions per partner set; for new rosters and trades this exceeds the sample, so the redistribution between components is partly guesswork until several weeks into the season.
combo_props#u4.what_would_resolve: Evaluate how many games a new combination needs before its rates beat the season average, then set shrinkage by roster age.

combo_props#u5.description: Crew assignments are published the morning of the game, and whether the free official assignment page exposes the referee list in machine-readable form was not verified, so the officiating link to free throws and minutes is open. The input nba.referee_crew is attached as context pending that check.
combo_props#u5.what_would_resolve: Test the NBA official referee assignment endpoint and archive timestamps.

combo_props#u6.description: Back-to-back, return-from-injury restrictions and clinched-seed rest affect minutes mixture weights but are tied to the unsettled load-management policy; no input here quantifies the policy for 2026-27.
combo_props#u6.what_would_resolve: Build a rest-probability model from the league's published player availability policy and history.

combo_props#u7.description: The protected clause does not say whether a starter counts as having entered the game in the first half or in the second half at the tip and at the third-quarter restart, so the rest-in-blowout void branch is unverified; the KXNBAPRAPROT secondary text is cut mid-sentence in the sampled rules, so any later sentences were not seen, and KXNBAPR/KXNBAPA wording is unsampled.
combo_props#u7.what_would_resolve: Sample rules_primary/secondary for the unprotected KXNBAPRA, KXNBAPR and KXNBAPA series and the full protected clause, and obtain a worked example from Kalshi support.

first_basket#u1.description: No first-basket scorer or first-team-to-score series is live for NBA and no rule text exists, so whether free throws, tip-ins or own-basket credit or goaltending count, what a non-playing named player resolves to, and what a game cancelled before any score resolves to are all unknown.
first_basket#u1.what_would_resolve: List the actual Kalshi first-basket series when they open and sample their rules_primary/secondary.

first_basket#u2.description: Opening-play labels (which set a coach called on the first possession) are only in paid play-type feeds or video, so the scripted-share model relies on proxies from first-six-minute usage.
first_basket#u2.what_would_resolve: Price a Synergy/Second Spectrum feed or label a sample of openers manually to test the proxy.

first_basket#u3.description: Whether the tip result is truly near 50/50 and how much jumper skill adds is only roughly known; the specific 0.1 slope used in the measurement is an assumption to be estimated.
first_basket#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate the tip-win logit on jumper tip history over 5 seasons from jump ball events.

first_basket#u4.description: The exposure of exact starting-lineup announcement times by free sources was not verified; if only post-game start flags are free, the pre-tip confirmation vintage must be captured live.
first_basket#u4.what_would_resolve: Check each free lineup source for time stamps and start a live capture if absent.

first_basket#u5.description: The existence of any NBA first-basket-scorer or first-team-to-score series on Kalshi is unverified: after the reconciliation the ledger has no series under this key at all, so every input rated primary or secondary here is conditional on such a contract appearing.
first_basket#u5.what_would_resolve: Re-pull the Kalshi series list for first-basket or first-score tickers, sample rules_primary/secondary, and otherwise treat this archetype as having no live contract.

game_moneyline_spread#u1.description: The recovered KXNBASPREAD text settles on the 'official final result' and uses half-point 'wins by more than X.5' strikes, but it does not say explicitly that overtime points count toward the margin, does not address Cup-final or play-in games, and does not say how a post-game score correction is handled.
game_moneyline_spread#u1.what_would_resolve: Read the full Kalshi rulebook for KXNBASPREAD or settled spread markets from overtime games.

game_moneyline_spread#u2.description: Whether free sources expose point-in-time EPM/RAPM values (as opposed to end-of-season values) was not verified; look-ahead in impact numbers would invalidate any backtest of the absence mechanics.
game_moneyline_spread#u2.what_would_resolve: Check vintage availability of DARKO/EPM history or compute own RAPM from play-by-play with a rolling window.

game_moneyline_spread#u3.description: Referee-crew influence on margin or home advantage is not established; crew effects on totals and foul rates are better supported, so a margin effect might not exist or be too small to estimate.
game_moneyline_spread#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate a crew random effect on margin residuals over 5 seasons and test significance.

game_moneyline_spread#u4.description: Minute-level availability decisions by coaches (resting a star in a blowout, rotation tightening) are not observed pregame, and the pool of recent comparable cases is small for each team.
game_moneyline_spread#u4.what_would_resolve: Build coach-level rotation priors from five seasons of minutes data and accept residual noise.

game_moneyline_spread#u5.description: Playoff single games inside a series use nba.series_game_conditional_state (elimination, adjustment and rest effects), a secondary input whose size is not estimated; series-level contracts are not filed in this archetype.
game_moneyline_spread#u5.what_would_resolve: Estimate the elimination and adjustment effects inside playoff series from 10 seasons of playoff games, and confirm the series_and_cup record owns the series-level tickers' inputs.

game_moneyline_spread#u6.description: Recalled magnitudes are unsourced: home-court value of about two points (it has declined in recent seasons), margin sd of about 12, and the 6% overall overtime rate; the regression targets should be re-estimated from 10 seasons of team-game logs.
game_moneyline_spread#u6.what_would_resolve: Estimate home advantage by season and the margin sd by pace bucket from game logs.

game_overtime_and_team_events#u1.description: The recovered head-to-head texts say 'in the full game' without stating that overtime counts and do not define bench (official non-starters vs a feed flag) or stat-correction handling; KXNBAOVERTIME and KXNBASERIESOT have no postponement or series-cancellation clause in their sampled text.
game_overtime_and_team_events#u1.what_would_resolve: Read Kalshi's full rulebook for these series or settled markets from overtime games and games with late starter changes.

game_overtime_and_team_events#u2.description: The excess factor kappa over the Gaussian tie mass (about 1.7-1.9) is recalled from the literature and not estimated here; a policy change in late-game fouling rules could shift it between seasons.
game_overtime_and_team_events#u2.what_would_resolve: Estimate kappa with isotonic regression on 15 seasons and check stability across rule changes.

game_overtime_and_team_events#u3.description: Intentional-foul tagging is not a flag in free play-by-play; it must be inferred from foul type and clock, which has a known misclassification rate.
game_overtime_and_team_events#u3.what_would_resolve: Validate an inference rule on a hand-labelled sample or buy tracked play-by-play with foul intent flags.

game_overtime_and_team_events#u4.description: Whether Kalshi's bench points use the official NBA starting five or a data vendor's starter flag (they differ for late lineup changes), and whether overtime is included, are not stated in the recovered KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS text.
game_overtime_and_team_events#u4.what_would_resolve: Read the rule text of any bench-points market and match the data source's starter flag.

game_overtime_and_team_events#u5.description: Rest, back-to-back and playoff rotation tightening change bench minutes; no input here converts schedule situation into bench share, and the effect may be confounded with blowout probability.
game_overtime_and_team_events#u5.what_would_resolve: Regress bench share on rest and playoff dummies controlling for margin using 5 seasons.

game_overtime_and_team_events#u6.description: KXNBASERIESOT is now known to be a count threshold (sampled '3+ games go to overtime' in the Finals), but whether other thresholds and earlier rounds are listed, and how an incomplete series (e.g. a cancelled game) settles, are not in the sampled text; the within-series correlation of close games that drives the 3+ tail is not estimated.
game_overtime_and_team_events#u6.what_would_resolve: Sample more KXNBASERIESOT markets across rounds and estimate the dispersion of OT-game counts per series from 20+ seasons of playoff series.

game_overtime_and_team_events#u7.description: Several magnitudes are recalled and not sourced: P(second OT | first OT) (stated near 0.07-0.10, plausibly 0.08-0.13), overtime points of 22-26 in total, and bench points near 35 (sd 8) with 90-100 bench minutes when close; the multi-overtime share in particular may be understated.
game_overtime_and_team_events#u7.what_would_resolve: Compute these from 15 seasons of line scores and box scores (period counts, starter flags) and replace the recalled values.

game_total#u1.description: The sampled total rule says 'total points are scored in the ... game' with no explicit overtime statement, so OT inclusion is inferred from 'official final result' and default box-score practice rather than verified; one overtime adds roughly 20-24 points, so the inference moves P(over) near the line.
game_total#u1.what_would_resolve: Read the full KXNBATOTAL rule text for any statement on overtime, or check settled markets for games that went to overtime.

game_total#u2.description: Whether the slower team controls tempo or pace composes additively is mixed in the literature; the composition coefficients are unestimated and may differ by era and rule changes (24-second reset after offensive rebound).
game_total#u2.what_would_resolve: Estimate the composition regression over several seasons and test for era effects.

game_total#u3.description: Transition-frequency and play-type data are paid (Synergy, Second Spectrum); free proxies from play-by-play (fast-break points) are crude, so the composition model has less information than the commercial feeds.
game_total#u3.what_would_resolve: Test whether free proxies recover the composition effect or price a tracking feed.

game_total#u4.description: Referee assignment availability and archive: assignments are posted on game day and history is available from third parties, but machine-readable official archives were not verified.
game_total#u4.what_would_resolve: Probe the official assignment page and snapshot daily.

game_total#u7.description: Unsourced magnitudes in the record: crew effect of about +/-3 points on totals at the extremes, game-level sd near 14 from shot noise (17-19 when including all components), the 1.5-2 point cross term, and the 24-point OT block; each is recalled, not estimated.
game_total#u7.what_would_resolve: Estimate crew effects from game logs with crew-season random effects, and the total sd and OT block from 10 seasons of team-game results.

game_win_margin#u1.description: Only one win-margin rule was sampled (KXNBAWINMARGIN, 6 to 10 points): the full band set, whether the top band is open-ended, and whether bands are listed for both sides are unseen, so band construction cannot be confirmed. Overtime inclusion in the settled margin is also unstated in the sampled rule text.
game_win_margin#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample every KXNBAWINMARGIN market in one game to list the band edges and sides.

game_win_margin#u2.description: The size of the OT/parity corrections to the margin pmf is recalled, not measured, and may vary with rule changes (the 2022-23 clutch rules, intentional foul rules).
game_win_margin#u2.what_would_resolve: Estimate the corrections on the last 10 seasons and test for structural breaks.

game_win_margin#u3.description: Clean identification of when each team's starters were pulled needs substitution-level data with correct clock parsing; free play-by-play has known timestamp errors.
game_win_margin#u3.what_would_resolve: Audit a sample of pull times by video or buy tracking data.

game_win_margin#u4.description: Seeding stakes and rest policy affect when coaches pull starters in lopsided games, but a measurable link from motivation to pull timing is not defined here.
game_win_margin#u4.what_would_resolve: Estimate pull time as a function of standing and schedule for each coach.

off_court_events#u1.description: All 16 series now have rules text, but several points are not stated: the identity of the 'Source Agencies' used by schedule, contract and joining markets; whether a re-signing with the current team counts as 'joining' a team for KXNBATEAMANNOUNCE; how a schedule change after the announcement affects KXNBAXMASOPPONENT; and the truncated tail of the KXNBANEXTCONTRACT and KXNBAAPOLOGY secondary texts.
off_court_events#u1.what_would_resolve: Read the full Kalshi rulebook / Source Agency list for these series and the untruncated rules_secondary text.

off_court_events#u2.description: Private negotiations, the content of owner and Board meetings and trade talks are unobservable; probabilities of expansion, relocation and trades rely on leaks and reference classes with few observations per event type.
off_court_events#u2.what_would_resolve: No public source; accept wide uncertainty or use reporter-reliability proxies; consider paid deal-intelligence services.

off_court_events#u3.description: The Board of Governors vote threshold for expansion awards and relocation (recalled as three-quarters of owners) and the typical durations from expansion process announcement to award are recalled from general knowledge and not verified from the current league constitution or recent decisions.
off_court_events#u3.what_would_resolve: Read the league constitution or credible coverage of recent approvals and tabulate dates.

off_court_events#u4.description: Expansion, European-league and conference-realignment markets have linked voting and negotiation dynamics (expansion in two cities forces realignment of one or two Western teams to the East) that the governance pipeline treats as separate events; the dependence between KXNBACITYEXPAND, KXNBAJOINCONF and KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE is not modelled.
off_court_events#u4.what_would_resolve: Build a joint scenario tree for expansion, realignment and European-league decisions from league statements and board calendars.

off_court_events#u5.description: Base rates pooled across event types hide heterogeneity; per-type inputs now exist for rule changes, top-10 pick trades, apologies, overseas signings and schedule pairings, but player-trade, relocation and retirement reference classes still rely on the pooled nba.offfield_base_rate with undefined window lengths.
off_court_events#u5.what_would_resolve: Choose reference classes per series family with a documented definition and test sensitivity.

off_court_events#u6.description: Several hazard numbers are recalled and unsourced: report-to-event conversion near 0.1 for talks and above 0.95 for an agreed report from a tier-one source, a retirement hazard of 20-25% per year at age 38+, stage completion rates (exploration about 0.2, definitive agreement about 0.9), and the Board-of-Governors approval threshold.
off_court_events#u6.what_would_resolve: Compile report stage versus outcome for 10 years of reported deals and retirements, and read the league constitution for the approval threshold.

off_court_events#u7.description: The maximum-contract tiers (25/30/35% of the cap by years of service), designated-veteran criteria and the projected cap used by nba.next_contract_value_model are recalled from the 2023 CBA and not re-read for the 2027 signing season.
off_court_events#u7.what_would_resolve: Read the current CBA maximum-salary article and the league's latest cap projection.

parlay_combo#u1.description: The live pack texts (KXNBAPREPACK2ML/3ML) contain no postponement, cancellation or void-leg clause, so the treatment of a postponed or cancelled leg is not stated; no same-game player/team combination series is live, so leg-void rules for player legs remain unknown.
parlay_combo#u1.what_would_resolve: Read Kalshi's full rulebook for the prepack series or a settled pack with a postponed leg.

parlay_combo#u2.description: Pairwise dependence between specific players' legs has too little data per pair (about 80 games per season), and sportsbook SGP correlations are proprietary; factor loadings by role are a pooled approximation.
parlay_combo#u2.what_would_resolve: Pool by role cells and validate on held-out seasons; no public source resolves pairwise dependence.

parlay_combo#u3.description: Whether a Gaussian copula with three factors captures tail dependence of hot-shooting nights is unproven; a t-copula or mixture may be needed and the choice affects extreme-leg combinations.
parlay_combo#u3.what_would_resolve: Compare Gaussian and t-copula log-likelihood on held-out joint outcomes.

parlay_combo#u4.description: How rest and schedule shocks create common minute reductions across legs is not defined, and the effect is confounded with the injury shock.
parlay_combo#u4.what_would_resolve: Define a rest-state indicator and test its loading on the minutes factor.

parlay_combo#u5.description: Whether a combination may contain nested or logically implied legs (spread cover with its moneyline, N+ with a lower N+, PRA with its components), how many legs are allowed and whether thresholds are fixed or chosen is unknown, and these determine whether degenerate dependence must be modelled.
parlay_combo#u5.what_would_resolve: Read the rules of any combination series once listed and record leg-count and composition limits.

parlay_combo#u6.description: Every same-game dependence figure is recalled and unsourced (within-team correlations of -0.1 to -0.3, margin-total correlation of 0.0-0.1, a spread knee near 6), and the near-zero cross-game dependence assumed for the live multi-game packs has not been measured.
parlay_combo#u6.what_would_resolve: Estimate same-game factor loadings and same-day cross-game residual correlation from 10 seasons of box scores.

parlay_combo#u7.description: The NHL leg of KXNBANHL needs a Stanley Cup probability that the NBA catalog does not define; until the NHL catalog's title model is wired in with a matching as-of timestamp, the pair cannot be valued from this record alone.
parlay_combo#u7.what_would_resolve: Link the NHL catalog's championship input by id and timestamp, or define a cross-sport input owned by both catalogs.

player_assists#u1.description: Whether free NBA.com tracking endpoints give potential assists and time of possession at game grain (not season totals) was not verified; if only season aggregates are free the per-game variation of creation volume must be estimated from play-by-play proxies. Specifically, leaguedashptstats is a season or per-game-average aggregate endpoint, game-level rows are only obtainable by single-date filtering (a workaround, not a documented game grain), and the recalled cross-game sd of about 25% of the mean potential-assist rate cannot be measured from free data.
player_assists#u1.what_would_resolve: Test the passing endpoint at game grain or confirm a paid feed.

player_assists#u2.description: Pass-lane quality and defender distance for assists are only in tracking data held by the league's providers; the model can only proxy them with shot type and teammates' shooting.
player_assists#u2.what_would_resolve: Price a Second Spectrum or Sportradar tracking feed or accept the proxy.

player_assists#u3.description: How much the unprotected contract's void at zero minutes selects the distribution (late scratches never play) versus the protected one is unquantified; the first-half-only void for KXNBAASTPROT is carried by nba.early_exit_hazard (same definition as in combo_props), whose rest-in-blowout component is estimated from play-by-play and not yet validated for guards.
player_assists#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate early-exit and zero-minute rates per player and test selection on realised hit rates.

player_assists#u4.description: The scorer-credit effect by arena is estimated from few seasons and may drift with scorer turnover; the size of the offset beyond half an assist is not established.
player_assists#u4.what_would_resolve: Estimate arena offsets over 6 seasons with shrinkage and test the stability.

player_assists#u5.description: Overtime assist inclusion in the settled count is not stated in the sampled KXNBAAST or KXNBAASTPROT text, and the KXNBAASTPROT secondary rules are truncated in the sampled rules text (cut mid-sentence after the second-half-entry clause), so its inactive-player and overtime wording is unseen.
player_assists#u5.what_would_resolve: Re-sample full rules_primary/rules_secondary for KXNBAASTPROT and confirm the overtime treatment of counted assists.

player_availability#u1.description: KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER has no rules text, so whether 'play together' means appearing in the same game or sharing court time, and the window, are not visible; the recovered KXNBARETURN and KXNBACOMPETE texts do not say how a suspension or a game protest/replay is handled.
player_availability#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample rules_primary and rules_secondary for KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER and read the full rulebook for KXNBARETURN/KXNBACOMPETE edge cases.

player_availability#u2.description: The archetype label says game-level starter or active status, but the live contracts are season-level and one-off; the game-level mechanism (30-minute confirmation, late scratch) has no live series, so its relevance is unclear.
player_availability#u2.what_would_resolve: Check whether game-level starter or active markets are listed during the season and re-file accordingly.

player_availability#u3.description: Every numeric prior in the stage and nonlinearity text is recalled and not verified against a dataset: incumbent starter retention (about 80%), the 20-30% of returns that slip past the stated date, and the status-to-play rates by label (Out near zero, Doubtful 0.05-0.25, Questionable 0.4-0.6, Probable 0.9+).
player_availability#u3.what_would_resolve: Compute each from 10 seasons of official injury and starter data.

player_availability#u4.description: Training-camp information (practice lineups, minute plans) is mostly closed and available only via reporter statements, so the opener signal rests on a small set of public cues.
player_availability#u4.what_would_resolve: Archive reporter statements systematically or accept coarse signals.

player_availability#u5.description: The base rate at which an unsigned veteran (age, prior minutes, injury history, public reputation) signs an NBA contract during a season is not estimated; the camp, injury-wave and buyout bumps in nba.unsigned_player_signing_hazard are qualitative.
player_availability#u5.what_would_resolve: Fit a discrete-time signing hazard on 10 seasons of unsigned veterans with age, last-season minutes and injury status as covariates.

player_availability#u6.description: KXNBACOMPETE counts 'any regular season game'; whether the NBA Cup championship game (which does not count toward regular-season records or statistics) counts as a regular-season game is not stated. The Cup exposure question earlier attached to the one-three accrual inputs moved with KXNBAONE3PT to season_stat_markets.
player_availability#u6.what_would_resolve: Read the full KXNBACOMPETE rules or a settled market involving a Cup-final appearance, and the NBA Cup rules on which games count as regular-season games.

player_escalator_payout#u1.description: The non-appearance treatment (inactive, never on court, early exit) and any protected variant of the escalator contracts are not visible in the sampled text; the points rules_primary is truncated at 600 characters and the rules_secondary does not address it, beyond saying that zero scored points pays Yes $0.00.
player_escalator_payout#u1.what_would_resolve: Re-sample the full rules_primary/secondary for KXNBAESCALATORPTS and KXNBAESCALATOR3PT, including a market for an inactive player, and confirm void versus zero-band treatment.

player_escalator_payout#u2.description: The beta-binomial dispersion (rho about 0.02-0.05) of within-game makes is recalled and its existence as skill-independent clustering is debated (hot-hand evidence is mixed); the tail depends on it.
player_escalator_payout#u2.what_would_resolve: Estimate rho over 5 seasons and test against a binomial with shot-quality adjustment.

player_escalator_payout#u3.description: Schedule-driven changes in heavy-minute probability (rest, back-to-back, playoff race) are not defined as an input, and could be confounded with closeness.
player_escalator_payout#u3.what_would_resolve: Add rest and standings terms to the heavy-minutes regression and test.

player_escalator_payout#u4.description: Closely matched tail events are rare, so a few hundred star games per season provide only a handful of observations in the top 1% for any one player, leaving the extreme tail dependent on pooling assumptions.
player_escalator_payout#u4.what_would_resolve: Pool across similar players and seasons; there is no public data that increases the sample.

player_escalator_payout#u5.description: Several numeric priors are recalled and not sourced: beta-binomial rho 0.02-0.05, a heavy-minutes component of 10-20% for stars, attempt sd 30-40% of the mean, a minutes-to-attempts correlation of 0.6-0.7, and a weight near 0.3 on recent make rate at 100 attempts.
player_escalator_payout#u5.what_would_resolve: Estimate each from 5 seasons of player-game shot logs and replace the recalled values.

player_free_throws#u1.description: The recovered KXNBAFTM rules are silent on whether overtime free throws count, whether technical, flagrant and clear-path free throws are included, how later stat corrections are handled, and what happens if the game is postponed or cancelled, or how a player ruled inactive before tip-off is treated (the text covers only an active player who never enters); only the 'N+' strike and the active-but-never-entered fair-price void are stated.
player_free_throws#u1.what_would_resolve: Read the full Kalshi market terms / rulebook for KXNBAFTM or settled examples with overtime or technical free throws.

player_free_throws#u2.description: Own and teammate availability is now attached via nba.injuries_pit and nba.teammate_absence_shift, but how a teammate's absence enters free-throw volume (a usage shift versus a change in drive and trip rate) is not set and has not been tested.
player_free_throws#u2.what_would_resolve: Attach nba.injuries_pit and nba.teammate_absence_shift and test their effect on trip rate.

player_free_throws#u3.description: Free play-by-play labels foul types but contact tagging for drive fouls and the identification of intentional fouls are inferred; accuracy of the inference was not tested.
player_free_throws#u3.what_would_resolve: Validate against a labelled sample or a paid contact-tagged feed.

player_free_throws#u4.description: The relation between free-throw percentage and three-point percentage for low-volume players is recalled (slope 0.5) and not estimated; the prior strength of 80 attempts is a placeholder.
player_free_throws#u4.what_would_resolve: Estimate on 10 seasons of players with at least 100 FTA and 100 3PA.

player_free_throws#u5.description: The live KXNBAFTM series is now verified (one sampled market, '5+' rung), but only one rules sample exists: the full rung set per player, whether low rungs (1+, 2+) are listed for low-volume players where zero-inflation dominates, and whether rule wording varies across seasons are not seen.
player_free_throws#u5.what_would_resolve: Sample rules_primary/secondary from several KXNBAFTM markets across dates and players and record the listed rung sets.

player_h2h_series_stats#u1.description: All 11 series have rules text, but the head-to-head texts say 'full game' without stating that overtime counts, and the leader texts do not say whether a player who enters only some games is compared on totals (assumed) or how a series ended early by forfeit would settle.
player_h2h_series_stats#u1.what_would_resolve: Read the full Kalshi rulebook for these series or settled H2H markets from overtime games.

player_h2h_series_stats#u2.description: Whether free NBA.com matchup data (who guarded whom) is available at playoff-game granularity, and the league identifier for Summer League box scores, were not verified. The nba_api leagueseasonmatchups endpoint is a season-type aggregate, so game-level playoff defender assignments are not shown to be available, and the 5-15% matchup shift is a recalled value; the input is therefore downgraded to context.
player_h2h_series_stats#u2.what_would_resolve: Query the matchup and Summer League endpoints for one past series and one past Summer League.

player_h2h_series_stats#u3.description: The correlation values by pair type (about -0.2 for teammates, +0.3 for opponents) are recalled expectations, not estimates; the sign for rebounds and assists across opponents may differ from that for points. The tie mass (12-20% for threes) and the series-length means (about 5.7 games for evenly matched teams, 4.8 for mismatched) are recalled from binomial arithmetic, not estimated from data.
player_h2h_series_stats#u3.what_would_resolve: Estimate pair-type correlations by stat on 5 seasons of box scores.

player_h2h_series_stats#u4.description: nba.player_shooting_regression is now attached for the compared stat, but how luck in threes or points is shrunk across the games of a series, and the strength of the regression for low-attempt shooters, is not defined or tested.
player_h2h_series_stats#u4.what_would_resolve: Attach nba.player_shooting_regression and test its effect on series-level totals.

player_h2h_series_stats#u5.description: With the leader tie rule now known ($1/N), the frequency of ties at the top for made threes and assists over a series, and the per-game correlation that drives every-game threes runs (2+ in every game), are not estimated; both move prices materially.
player_h2h_series_stats#u5.what_would_resolve: Estimate tie-at-top frequencies and per-game hit correlations from 20 seasons of playoff series player game logs.

player_milestones#pm-boxscore-endpoint-s.description: The player-game box-score dataset names nba_api boxscoretraditionalv2 as free_scrape. This resolver could not confirm that V2 box-score endpoints stay populated for 2026-27 (v3 successors exist), so the endpoint name and field list are unverified.
player_milestones#pm-boxscore-endpoint-s.what_would_resolve: Call boxscoretraditionalv3 and the cdn.nba.com liveData boxscore for one completed 2026-27 game and confirm minutes and the five category fields.

player_milestones#pm-fair-price-definiti.description: The sampled KXNBA2D/KXNBA3D rules say an inactive or never-entered player settles 'to a fair price' without defining it. Only the protected rebound contract (KXNBAREBPROT) ties it to 'the fair price prior to the opening tip', which would already embed P(inactive). So the refund payout may not equal par, and whether any value is lost or gained on a void is not stated.
player_milestones#pm-fair-price-definiti.what_would_resolve: Pull the full Kalshi rulebook definition of 'fair price' and settle history for a voided DD/TD market to see the realised payout relative to the pre-tip price.

player_milestones#pm-ot-inclusion.description: The sampled rules_secondary states what counts as a double/triple double and the void rule but does not say whether overtime statistics are included; the text sample is also truncated before the sources agencies are named.
player_milestones#pm-ot-inclusion.what_would_resolve: Pull the full rules_secondary / contract PDF for KXNBA2D and KXNBA3D and confirm OT and the source agency; check one settled OT game.

player_milestones#pm-playoff3d-scope.description: KXNBAPLAYOFF3D is read as at least one triple-double in any 2026 playoff game, but the text does not say whether Play-In games count as playoff games (other NBA series exclude them explicitly), nor whether overtime statistics count, nor what happens if the player is traded or ruled out for the playoffs before they start.
player_milestones#pm-playoff3d-scope.what_would_resolve: Check a settled KXNBAPLAYOFF3D market for a player whose team played in the Play-In, and request the full rules_secondary for the source agency and overtime wording.

player_milestones#pm-situational-gap.description: No input captures second-night-of-back-to-back, minutes-restriction ramp-ups after injury and playoff-seeding rest on star DD probability beyond what projected minutes absorb, so a systematic minutes error would pass through undetected.
player_milestones#pm-situational-gap.what_would_resolve: Compare realized minutes versus pregame projection by rest state and clinch status to see whether a separate variable is needed.

player_milestones#pm-stat-chase-size.description: Whether teammate gifting near 10 is a real, coach-specific behaviour large enough to be estimated, or noise; no verified public estimate exists and the sample of 8-9 count late-blowout situations per player is small.
player_milestones#pm-stat-chase-size.what_would_resolve: Estimate from 3 seasons of play-by-play pooled across coaches with empirical Bayes and test out-of-sample whether the multiplier differs from 1.

player_milestones#pm-tracking-access.description: Rebound chances, contested boards and potential assists come from tracking data (Second Spectrum / NBA tracking) that is only partly public; the free endpoints expose aggregates, not event-level chances with timestamps.
player_milestones#pm-tracking-access.what_would_resolve: Confirm which hustle/tracking dashboards are queryable per game; otherwise buy a licensed feed.

player_points#pp-bucket-mixing.description: After the reconciliation the archetype still mixes single-player ladders with a bench-points series (KXNBABENCHPTS) whose entity (team sum or a player as a bench unit) is unverified; the bench series' definition of bench and its settlement are inferred from the title only.
player_points#pp-bucket-mixing.what_would_resolve: Sample KXNBABENCHPTS rules and confirm whether it is a team bench total or a player contract; if a team total, it sits beside the game_overtime bench inputs.

player_points#pp-defender-distance.description: The shot-quality input no longer needs per-shot closest-defender distance: shotchartdetail returns location, zone, action type and distance, not defender distance. Whether the tracking dashboards expose aggregate closest-defender bins by shot type for 2026-27 is unverified here, and a defender-distance-by-location cross may require paid tracking data.
player_points#pp-defender-distance.what_would_resolve: Query shotchartdetail and the player tracking shot dashboards for one player-season and list the fields; if defender bins are absent, price a licensed tracking feed.

player_points#pp-ot-inclusion.description: The sampled KXNBAPTS and KXNBAPTSPROT texts do not state whether overtime points count for the ladder (the protected text mentions overtime only when defining a second-half appearance). The record assumes the official final box score, which usually includes OT; KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE (season_stat_markets) says 'including overtime' explicitly, so absence of that phrase here is ambiguous.
player_points#pp-ot-inclusion.what_would_resolve: Read the full rulebook for the points ladders and check a settled overtime game to see whether overtime points were included.

player_points#pp-situational.description: No input models stars' rest-for-seeding and minutes-restriction behaviour that is not in the injury report, yet it changes minute scenarios in late regular season.
player_points#pp-situational.what_would_resolve: Back-test minutes error by clinch status and rest days to see if a dedicated variable is needed.

player_points#pp-titleonly.description: KXNBALADDERPTS and KXNBABENCHPTS are TITLE_ONLY: whether the ladder series shares the KXNBAPTS void rule, and what counts as bench points (official starter flag, team or player entity), are inferred, not read.
player_points#pp-titleonly.what_would_resolve: Sample rules_primary and rules_secondary for the three TITLE_ONLY series and replace the inferred statements with verbatim quotes.

player_rebounds#pr-leakage-source.description: The team-rebound count per game is assumed to be available in team box scores; whether player-credited versus team rebounds can be separated from public play-by-play is not verified here. The 6-10% leakage figure used in the creditable-pool rationale is a hypothesis with no source and must be estimated, not assumed.
player_rebounds#pr-leakage-source.what_would_resolve: Pull one game from the play-by-play and box-score endpoints and reconcile team rebounds.

player_rebounds#pr-ot-inclusion.description: The KXNBAREB and KXNBAREBPROT texts settle on 'the player's rebounds recorded' without saying whether overtime rebounds count; the protected text mentions overtime only when defining a second-half appearance.
player_rebounds#pr-ot-inclusion.what_would_resolve: Check settled KXNBAREB markets from overtime games against regulation-only and full box-score rebound counts.

player_rebounds#pr-situational.description: No input handles rest-for-seeding and post-injury minutes ramp-ups that change bigs' minutes; the effect may be large for specific stars but is not quantified.
player_rebounds#pr-situational.what_would_resolve: Back-test projected-minutes error by rest state and clinch status.

player_rebounds#pr-tracking-access.description: Rebound chances, contested-board fractions and box-out counts come from optical tracking that is licensed (Second Spectrum) and only partly exposed in public dashboards; the existing reb_chances and tracking inputs may therefore be unmeasurable without payment. Even where public tracking dashboards exist they are season or split aggregates, not per-game rows with as-of timestamps, and per-game vintages are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; reb_chances may therefore exist only at season grain, in which case rebound-chance share must fall back to box-score rebounds per minute and nba.rebound_pool.
player_rebounds#pr-tracking-access.what_would_resolve: List which hustle/tracking endpoints return per-game player rows; otherwise price a licensed feed.

player_threes#p3-assist-linkage.description: nba.assisted_three_passer_map assumes every made three in the free play-by-play feed carries the assisting player id, and that missed threes can be linked to the intended passer. Assist ids exist on made shots, but missed-shot passer linkage is not available in box scores and may be absent in the feed.
player_threes#p3-assist-linkage.what_would_resolve: Parse one season of playbyplayv3 and compare made-three counts with assisted counts against the official box-score assist totals; test whether any missed-shot passer field exists.

player_threes#p3-defender-distance.description: Per-shot closest-defender distance is believed not to be returned by shotchartdetail, so make-probability and openness inputs are rebased on zone and action type with defender distance only as aggregate dashboard bins. Whether those bins exist per date window for 2026-27, and whether a catch-and-shoot by defender-distance cross is public, is unverified.
player_threes#p3-defender-distance.what_would_resolve: Query shotchartdetail and the tracking shot dashboards with a DateTo filter for one player and team and list returned fields and bins.

player_threes#p3-hothand.description: Whether within-game shooting form is persistent enough (hot hand) to alter later attempts or makes beyond team-level shocks is unresolved in the literature and is not modelled by any input.
player_threes#p3-hothand.what_would_resolve: Estimate within-game autocorrelation in make results conditional on shot difficulty from tracking data over multiple seasons.

player_threes#p3-ot-inclusion.description: The KXNBA3PT and KXNBA3PTPROT texts settle on 'the player's made three-pointers recorded' without saying whether overtime makes count; the protected text mentions overtime only when defining a second-half appearance. The record assumes the official box score including OT.
player_threes#p3-ot-inclusion.what_would_resolve: Read the full rules or a settled KXNBA3PT market from an overtime game in which the player made threes in OT.

player_threes#p3-situational.description: No variable captures rest and travel effects on shooting makes or rest-for-seeding minute cuts; magnitude for threes is unknown.
player_threes#p3-situational.what_would_resolve: Back-test residual 3P% by rest and schedule state.

player_threes#p3-titleonly.description: The ladder series KXNBALADDER3PT is TITLE_ONLY; whether its markets are cumulative 'N+' rungs with the KXNBA3PT void rule, or a different strike construction, is unknown.
player_threes#p3-titleonly.what_would_resolve: Sample KXNBALADDER3PT rules_primary/rules_secondary and compare strike_type and floor_strike with KXNBA3PT.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-2h-ot-split.description: Each text is explicit (KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL include overtime; KXNBA2HWINNER says the 2nd half 'does not include overtime'), so this is not a wording gap; what is open is that one simulated game must yield both a regulation-only and an OT-inclusive second-half margin, and no input states how the two are produced jointly.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-2h-ot-split.what_would_resolve: Define the OT-inclusive 2H margin as regulation 2H margin plus an OT increment drawn from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin, and check settled KXNBA2H and KXNBA2HWINNER markets from one overtime game.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-lineup-data.description: Lineup-level possession and rating data with enough history for ridge-based unit ratings requires either pbpstats or a licensed feed; free coverage is partial and heavily rate limited.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-lineup-data.what_would_resolve: Evaluate coverage of pbpstats and nba_api lineup endpoints over a sample of games.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-live-state.description: Q2, Q3, Q4 and 2H markets exist for the same game as Q1, and the sampled rules give no close or trading-stop time. If they trade after tipoff, the needed inputs include in-game state (score at period start, who is on court, foul and bonus state, time remaining), which no input here covers; if they close at tipoff, pregame information suffices.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-live-state.what_would_resolve: Read the market close_time and trading hours for later-period markets on a live event and check whether quotes move after the first tip; then add a live-state input set if they do.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-q3-effect.description: Whether coaches have persistent second-half (Q3) adjustment effects larger than noise is unsettled; estimated effects are typically heavily shrunk and may be indistinguishable from zero.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-q3-effect.what_would_resolve: Estimate the variance component of coach Q3 effects across seasons and test out-of-sample persistence.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-start-timing.description: nba.starters_pit is KEEP_PRIMARY for Q1 and Q3 because starters are confirmed about 30 minutes before tipoff, but the sampled markets for Nov 8 games already show status active and no close time is sampled, so it is unknown whether the lineup confirmation arrives before the market stops trading.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-start-timing.what_would_resolve: Compare the starter-confirmation timestamp with each period market's close time over a sample of games and record the lead time.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-strike-const.description: Sampled period strikes (1st quarter total over 71.5, 2nd quarter total over 70.5) sit far above typical combined quarter scores, suggesting ladders or placeholder rungs; which strikes are live and how a threshold relates to the central value is unknown.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-strike-const.what_would_resolve: Capture the full strike list per event and compare with realised period totals.

quarter_and_half_markets#qh-titleonly.description: KXNBA1QTEAMTOTAL and KXNBA4QTEAMTOTAL are TITLE_ONLY, so their overtime treatment (the 4Q one is the only team total where it could matter) and void wording are inferred from sibling series. The sampled spread, total and tie texts also print no postponement or cancellation sentence, unlike the game-level props.
quarter_and_half_markets#qh-titleonly.what_would_resolve: Sample rules for the two TITLE_ONLY team totals and the full rules_secondary of one quarter spread/total to read postponement handling.

race_to_and_points_leader#rl-coaching-ga.description: Opening scripted plays and the timing of first substitutions for the stars are coach specific but not measured by any input; their effect on a race to 30 (the sampled N) is unquantified.
race_to_and_points_leader#rl-coaching-ga.what_would_resolve: Estimate coach effects on first-stint points per possession from play-by-play and test persistence.

race_to_and_points_leader#rl-no-rules.description: Rules are now sampled for KXNBARACE and KXNBAPTSLEADER, but neither states whether overtime points count toward the leader nor what happens if no team reaches N; the sample shows only N = 30 for the race, so the set of listed N values is unknown.
race_to_and_points_leader#rl-no-rules.what_would_resolve: Sample several KXNBARACE events to list the N values offered and read the full rules for an explicit overtime and never-reached clause.

race_to_and_points_leader#rl-officiating.description: Whether the officiating crew's early foul calls alter the first-to-N result or the star's minutes is unmeasured and no input represents it.
race_to_and_points_leader#rl-officiating.what_would_resolve: Test whether crew foul rate predicts early free-throw runs in the first stint.

race_to_and_points_leader#rl-race-scope.description: KXNBARACE is a single-game team race to N (sample N = 30), so the per-game first-passage table applies. Still open: whether player-based race variants or N values above 30 are listed, where the first-passage table (N in 5-30) would need extrapolation.
race_to_and_points_leader#rl-race-scope.what_would_resolve: Enumerate KXNBARACE events across a week of games to list the N values and confirm no player-based race series exists.

race_to_and_points_leader#rl-tie-rule.description: The tie rule is now known (Yes pays $1/N among tied leaders), but the frequency of a tied maximum is an unverified estimate; with about 20 players and integer points, ties among the top two scorers are frequent enough to move fair prices for near-equal stars, and nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank must handle them per the 1/N rule.
race_to_and_points_leader#rl-tie-rule.what_would_resolve: Compute the historical share of games with a tied points maximum, by gap in pregame expected points, from 5 seasons of box scores.

season_futures_team#sf-cup-rule.description: The rule that Cup games before the final count in the regular season is read on KXNBAPOSTASREC but not on KXNBAWINS, KXNBARECORD or the division contracts; the scheduling of filler games for teams eliminated in the Cup group stage (opponent, venue, date) in 2026-27 is assumed, not verified.
season_futures_team#sf-cup-rule.what_would_resolve: Read the league's 2026-27 Cup and schedule-completion rules and version the remaining schedule when filler games are announced.

season_futures_team#sf-injury-data.description: A structured, point-in-time injury history with return dates over many seasons is not available as a clean public dataset; hazards would have to be built from archived reports and transaction lists.
season_futures_team#sf-injury-data.what_would_resolve: Evaluate coverage of Pro Sports Transactions plus an own capture of daily reports going forward.

season_futures_team#sf-mixed-bucket.description: Beyond the team simulation the bucket holds one award vote (the regular-season MVP inside KXNBAMVPCHAMP); the MVP vote's dependence on team record is not estimated by any fitted input yet.
season_futures_team#sf-mixed-bucket.what_would_resolve: Fit the MVP conditional logit with team win percentage as a covariate on 20 seasons of voting results.

season_futures_team#sf-seed-tie-edge.description: KXNBAEAST1SEED/KXNBAWEST1SEED and KXNBASEEDOU state no tie rule of their own (division texts explicitly defer to league tiebreaks); the record assumes the official seed after tiebreaks, and KXNBAPLAYOFFWINS states no treatment of a series not completed.
season_futures_team#sf-seed-tie-edge.what_would_resolve: Confirm on a settled seed market from a season with a tie at the boundary that the official tiebroken seed was used.

season_futures_team#sf-tiebreak-and-divi.description: Division, 1-seed and seed contracts defer to 'the governing league's official tie-breaking rules' without listing them; the 2026-27 two-team and multi-team order is assumed from past seasons. Five division contracts arrived from the unregistered record, which modelled them with nba.division_race_tiebreak_state, a duplicate of nba.tiebreak_ledger used here.
season_futures_team#sf-tiebreak-and-divi.what_would_resolve: Code the league's 2026-27 tiebreak document into nba.tiebreak_ledger, test on past tied divisions and mark nba.division_race_tiebreak_state DUPLICATE_OF it in the catalog.

season_futures_team#sf-titleonly.description: Only KXNBANEWCHAMP is TITLE_ONLY (31 of 32 series have rules); it is presumably the same event as KXNBAFIRSTTIMECHAMP or KXNBANEWCHAMPION, but which franchise list it uses is unknown. KXNBAMOSTWINS and KXNBAWINS state no rule for a shortened season.
season_futures_team#sf-titleonly.what_would_resolve: Sample KXNBANEWCHAMP rules and compare its franchise list with KXNBAFIRSTTIMECHAMP and KXNBANEWCHAMPION.

season_stat_markets#ss-coaching-gap.description: Mid-season coaching changes and rest policies can redefine a star's role and minutes; the size of this effect on season stat races is not measured by any input.
season_stat_markets#ss-coaching-gap.what_would_resolve: Backtest minutes and usage changes following coaching changes over several seasons.

season_stat_markets#ss-gamespecials-scop.description: KXNBAGAMESPECIALS is a mixed specials series: the sampled event is 15+ steals plus blocks by any player, but its secondary text refers to quarter-specific markets that exclude overtime, so other events in the series may be quarter-level or other stat combinations needing different inputs.
season_stat_markets#ss-gamespecials-scop.what_would_resolve: Enumerate the events listed under KXNBAGAMESPECIALS and classify each by stat, window (game or quarter) and overtime treatment.

season_stat_markets#ss-low-volume-three-.description: For KXNBAONE3PT the subject is a player with near-zero three-point attempts; nba.three_volume's beta prior (about 200-300 attempts of weight, career/team based) is not defined for players with almost no attempts, and whether attempts are a skill or a coaching permission is unclear.
season_stat_markets#ss-low-volume-three-.what_would_resolve: Fit a hierarchical zero-inflated attempt model by position and coach on 10 seasons of low-volume bigs and check calibration of 'at least one make' outcomes.

season_stat_markets#ss-no-live-series.description: Ten of the twelve series now filed here have rules text, but KXNBAHIGHESTSCORING (player with the highest scoring game, presumably an argmax over season maxima with an unknown tie rule) and KXNBAPLAYERSPECIALS (mixed player specials) are TITLE_ONLY, so their settlement and inputs are unknown.
season_stat_markets#ss-no-live-series.what_would_resolve: Sample rules for KXNBAHIGHESTSCORING and KXNBAPLAYERSPECIALS; if the former is an argmax over season-high games, extend nba.single_game_ceiling_tail to a maximum over candidates.

season_stat_markets#ss-ownership-overlap.description: Team run-length contracts now all sit here (KXNBAWINSTREAK, KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK, KXNBALASTTOLOSE) while season win totals, records and KXNBAMOSTWINS sit in season_futures_team; both need the same simulated season, and nba.team_win_streak_hazard and nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model overlap (one any-team threshold, one argmax with ties) without a shared simulation definition.
season_stat_markets#ss-ownership-overlap.what_would_resolve: Define one shared regular-season path simulation referenced by both archetypes and record the two streak inputs as views of it.

season_stat_markets#ss-rules-versioning.description: Scorer-credit practices for steals and blocks (home-arena generosity) matter for the 15-stocks contract and the source agencies' rounding (decimal places, half-up) and late stat corrections matter for averages near the strike; neither is confirmed for 2026-27.
season_stat_markets#ss-rules-versioning.what_would_resolve: Read the Source Agencies' published rounding and correction policy and estimate arena-level steal and block credit effects from play-by-play.

series_and_cup#sc-archetype-mismatch.description: After the reconciliation the archetype is playoff-series paths plus the Cup; the Cup group and knockout contracts share no mechanism with best-of-seven paths beyond team strength, and two series contracts (30-point comeback, 40-point blowout) need in-game score data unlike the rest.
series_and_cup#sc-archetype-mismatch.what_would_resolve: Split Cup contracts into their own archetype with the Cup inputs, or keep them here with a separate stage and data set as now.

series_and_cup#sc-coaching-gap.description: Coach decisions on playoff rotation shortening, in-series adjustments, resting stars once a series is decided and Cup margin management are not measured by any input, yet they shift series paths and Cup tiebreaks.
series_and_cup#sc-coaching-gap.what_would_resolve: Estimate coach-level game-to-game margin residuals within playoff series and Cup margin-chasing in final group games from play-by-play.

series_and_cup#sc-comeback-definition.description: KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK's text says 'overcome a deficit of at least 30 points and win' without saying whether the deficit is measured at any moment including overtime, and KXNBAPOLOSE is titled 'exactly 7 losses' while its strike_type is greater_or_equal, so the strike construction of the losses ladder is ambiguous.
series_and_cup#sc-comeback-definition.what_would_resolve: Check settled KXNBAPOLOSE markets (exact versus at-least payout) and a settled KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK market against play-by-play maximum deficits.

series_and_cup#sc-cup-bracket-structure.description: nba.cup_finals_pair_probability assumes the Cup knockout bracket is split by conference so the Finals pair is one East and one West team, with semifinals and final at one neutral site; the current season's bracket, seeding of wildcards and venue rules are not verified here, and a shared site adds correlation the product formula ignores.
series_and_cup#sc-cup-bracket-structure.what_would_resolve: Read the league's 2026-27 Cup format document and record bracket halves, wildcard seeding and venues; bound the pair probability under a copula.

series_and_cup#sc-ot-venue-silence.description: None of the series texts addresses overtime (relevant to KXNBAFINBLOWOUT margins and 30-point comebacks), a game relocated to a neutral site (road-win and home-clinch definitions use home/away), or a series not completed; the record assumes official final results including overtime.
series_and_cup#sc-ot-venue-silence.what_would_resolve: Request full rules_secondary for KXNBAFINBLOWOUT, KXNBASERIESROADWINS and KXNBAHOMECLINCH and check settlements of overtime Finals games.

series_and_cup#sc-ownership-overlap.description: Series-length and bracket machinery is defined here (nba.series_length_distribution, nba.playoff_round_event_counts) and also consumed by season_futures_team (titles, playoff wins), player_milestones (KXNBAPLAYOFF3D) and the playoff-points record; each references catalog ids, but no single bracket simulation is defined as the shared source.
series_and_cup#sc-ownership-overlap.what_would_resolve: Define one shared playoff bracket simulation input referenced by every archetype that consumes series lengths or advancement.

series_and_cup#sc-titleonly.description: 23 of 24 series have rules text; KXNBAPLAYOFFHOMEGAMES is TITLE_ONLY and shares its title with KXNBAPLAYOFFHOST ('NBA Team Home Playoff Games'), so it is presumably the same count, but whether it also requires games 'actually hosted' and excludes the Play-In is not read.
series_and_cup#sc-titleonly.what_would_resolve: Sample KXNBAPLAYOFFHOMEGAMES rules and compare with the KXNBAPLAYOFFHOST text.

steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-credit-bias-.description: The size of arena-level scorer bias in steal and block credit is asserted in the existing catalog but I have no verified estimate; it could be too small to matter against Poisson noise. The extra dispersion index of 0.1-0.2 used in stage s4 is an unverified hypothesis, not an estimate.
steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-credit-bias-.what_would_resolve: Estimate arena fixed effects on steals and blocks over 5 seasons controlling for team and opponent.

steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-hustle-acces.description: Deflections, contests and rim-protection tracking are the best drivers of steals and blocks, but per-game player rows (versus season aggregates from leaguehustlestatsplayer and the defensive dashboards) are not confirmed public through nba_api, and the game-level boxscorehustlev2 and per-game shots-defended-at-rim fields are unverified. nba.deflection_rate and nba.rim_contest_volume_on_court are therefore secondary until confirmed, and may need paid Second Spectrum data or fall back to season grain.
steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-hustle-acces.what_would_resolve: Query the hustle box score and shot-defense endpoints for a sample game and list returned fields.

steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-no-turnover-.description: The archetype is named for turnovers but no turnover series exists in the ledger; if a turnover market appears its rules (player turnovers as official stat, OT) are unknown. Consequently no input here models a player's OWN turnovers (handler load, usage, pressure faced); nba.turnover_pressure and nba.live_ball_turnover_profile describe steal supply for the defender only.
steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-no-turnover-.what_would_resolve: Re-check the live Kalshi series list for a player-turnovers series and sample its rules.

steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-ot-inclusion.description: The sampled KXNBASTL, KXNBABLK and KXNBASTOCK rules state the settlement statistic but never say whether overtime counts; the model assumes the official final box score (which includes OT) without confirmation, and the ladder tail changes in the roughly 6% of games that go to overtime.
steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-ot-inclusion.what_would_resolve: Read the full rulebook for the steals and blocks ladders and check one settled overtime game for whether OT steals or blocks were counted.

steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-situational.description: Fatigue on back-to-backs and post-injury minute ramps may change activity-based events (deflections, contests) more than scoring, but no input measures that effect.
steals_blocks_turnovers#sbt-situational.what_would_resolve: Back-test deflections per 36 by rest state.

summer_league_games#sl-announcement-data.description: Game-day announcements of who plays have no structured archive and are published informally; a point-in-time dataset would have to be captured live, and there is no free historical record for calibration. Consequently nba.news and nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard are secondary, not primary, until the announcement-to-participation map can be calibrated.
summer_league_games#sl-announcement-data.what_would_resolve: Start live capture of team and beat-writer announcements with timestamps for the next Summer League.

summer_league_games#sl-efficiency-gap.description: Shooting-efficiency regression for low-sample rookies is not captured; how to shrink a rookie's shooting to a talent prior given college-to-NBA three-point line change is undefined.
summer_league_games#sl-efficiency-gap.what_would_resolve: Fit a shooting translation model on college and G League shooting data for historical rookies.

summer_league_games#sl-event-effects.description: Whether venue (Las Vegas vs Salt Lake altitude), crowd and event differences change scoring and minutes beyond team rosters is unquantified.
summer_league_games#sl-event-effects.what_would_resolve: Estimate event fixed effects on pace and scoring from past results.

summer_league_games#sl-format-facts.description: The current Summer League game length, overtime procedure and foul rules are assumed to differ from regulation NBA rules but I have not verified the present values.
summer_league_games#sl-format-facts.what_would_resolve: Read the league's published Summer League rules for the current year.

summer_league_games#sl-no-series.description: All eight Summer League series have rules text, but the game, spread and total texts do not say whether overtime points count or how a cancelled game settles, the MVP text names no voting body or co-winner rule, and only the first-half winner text gives a tie and postponement rule.
summer_league_games#sl-no-series.what_would_resolve: Check settled KXNBASUMMERTOTAL and KXNBASUMMERSPREAD markets from an overtime Summer League game and request the full rules_secondary for the source agency.

team_total#tt-environment-gap.description: No input represents venue effects on scoring (altitude, shooting backdrop); the magnitude for specific arenas could matter for team totals and is untested.
team_total#tt-environment-gap.what_would_resolve: Estimate arena fixed effects on points per possession controlling for teams.

team_total#tt-ot-inclusion.description: The sampled rules never mention overtime and the existing draft claims OT is included per rules; if OT counts, a 6% mixture of about a dozen extra points shifts tail probabilities, if not the settlement is regulation-only. No input builds a regulation-only versus overtime-included alternative except nba.ot_model as context; the tail version of nba.team_points_variance_by_style outputs both.
team_total#tt-ot-inclusion.what_would_resolve: Read the full contract terms and test one settled OT game's result.

team_total#tt-schedule-gap.description: Back-to-back and rest effects on a team's offensive efficiency and pace are not represented, and published estimates of their size vary.
team_total#tt-schedule-gap.what_would_resolve: Back-test residual team points on rest differential over several seasons.

team_total#tt-strike-ladder.description: The sampled strike (135.5 for Oklahoma City) is far above a typical team total, which suggests ladders with multiple strikes; which strikes exist and whether team totals are listed at the main number is unknown. For far-away rungs the upper tail of team points (three-point variance, overtime) matters more than the mean, which is why nba.team_points_variance_by_style now outputs tail quantiles.
team_total#tt-strike-ladder.what_would_resolve: Capture the full strike set per event from the Kalshi API.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u1.description: KXNBAALLSTAR (2025) and KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS have only a one-line rules_primary: format, ties, non-participation of a named team and source of truth are unstated; KXNBAALLSTARGAME is silent on the tiebreak after point differential and on ties in 12-minute games.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u1.what_would_resolve: Sample current-year rules for these series or obtain Kalshi's clarification of the tie and team-change branches.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u10.description: Shooting Stars format (team size, locations and point values, time limit, rounds, ties) is absent from the rules text, so nba.shooting_stars_team_skill cannot simulate scores yet.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u10.what_would_resolve: Read the league's 2026 Shooting Stars format release and the Kalshi market page for that event.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u2.description: Format details not in rules text are from memory: 3PT ball values (money balls, deep-zone balls) and rack count, dunk judging scale and dunk-off rule, 2025 ASG four-team target-score format, and the 2026 round-robin tiebreak after point differential.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u2.what_would_resolve: Read the league's official format releases for each event-year and record each field in the format ledger with provenance.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u3.description: Ball-by-ball contest data and per-dunk judge scores are not provided in a structured public table, so the round-score correlation and judge model would rely on hand coding of video.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u3.what_would_resolve: Locate a structured source or hand-code recent contests to sizes sufficient to estimate rho and judge effects.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u4.description: The effect of effort, prize incentives and fatigue on exhibition play is not measurable with any pregame variable defined here and the sample of games under the current format is very small.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u4.what_would_resolve: Collect more seasons under the current format and test candidate effort proxies such as late-game defence rate.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u5.description: The Celebrity Game was removed from contract_types because no live Kalshi series exists in the evidence pack; if one is listed it needs roster-composition and special-scoring inputs.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u5.what_would_resolve: Check the Kalshi series list each All-Star cycle and add an archetype or stage if a Celebrity Game series appears.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u6.description: Per-judge dunk scores (needed for the judge effect) may exist only on broadcast video, and combine verticals are missing for undrafted or G League dunk entrants; structured availability is unverified.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u6.what_would_resolve: Check NBA.com recaps, NBA Stats event pages and video for per-judge cards for 2015-2026 and count entrants lacking combine data.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u7.description: Contest entrants who also play Rising Stars or the All-Star Game (fatigue, reduced effort), home-market entrants and crowd influence on dunk judges are unmodelled for the skills contests.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u7.what_would_resolve: Tag past entrants by doubling-up and home-market status and test score residuals in the contest models.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u8.description: No existing blueprint fits the seven disjoint processes (game_side is chosen as nearest for the team tournaments); inputs are scoped per series in catalog_entry and contract.series_input_scope instead of splitting the archetype.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u8.what_would_resolve: Decide whether to split into contests, team exhibitions and MVP archetypes or add an exhibition blueprint.

unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u9.description: All-Star MVP selection method (media panel size, any fan-vote component) and whether it covers the championship game or the whole tournament are not in the rules and are unverified for the 2026 format.
unreg:all_star_weekend_events#u9.what_would_resolve: Read the NBA's MVP announcement and voting description for 2025 and 2026 and store it in the format ledger.

unreg:series_cumulative_points#u1.description: Neither KXNBASERIESTOTALPTS nor KXNBASERIESPTSSPREAD rules mention overtime; 'cumulative points scored throughout the series' probably means official final scores including OT, but this is not stated.
unreg:series_cumulative_points#u1.what_would_resolve: Kalshi rulebook entry for these series or a settled market where an OT game decided the rung.

unreg:series_cumulative_points#u2.description: Treatment of an incomplete series (cancelled or forfeited game), the named source of truth, and whether the total settles early once the running sum crosses the strike are not in the sampled rules.
unreg:series_cumulative_points#u2.what_would_resolve: Full contract terms document for the series markets, or Kalshi support confirmation.

unreg:series_cumulative_points#u3.description: Only one Finals series was sampled per ticker; earlier rounds may list different strikes, mirror markets for the other team or negative spreads, and the spread orientation convention is unknown. Only the Finals event KXNBASERIESPTSSPREAD-26NYKSASFIN and KXNBASERIESTOTALPTS-26NYKSASFIN were sampled, so whether earlier rounds list these series at all is also unverified and claims about integer strikes, ties and other rounds are conditional.
unreg:series_cumulative_points#u3.what_would_resolve: Sample rules and strikes of first-round to conference-finals markets for both series tickers.

unreg:series_cumulative_points#u4.description: The within-series correlation of totals and margins and the game-number drift are estimated from about fifteen series per season; their size, and whether they changed with the recent three-point era, is uncertain.
unreg:series_cumulative_points#u4.what_would_resolve: Random-effects fit on 2004+ playoffs with era interaction and posterior intervals; out-of-sample check on recent seasons.

unreg:series_cumulative_points#u5.description: It is not verified that official.nba.com keeps a historical archive of playoff referee assignments with announcement times, which the whistle-regime input needs for its point-in-time rule.
unreg:series_cumulative_points#u5.what_would_resolve: Check the archive depth of the assignments page or confirm officials per game from Basketball-Reference box scores.

unreg:series_cumulative_points#u6.description: Series id and game number as structured fields in NBA Stats leaguegamelog are not confirmed; they probably have to be derived from game id, date and team pairs (the playoff game id may encode round, series and game but this was not checked), and Basketball-Reference series pages would need scraping. The random-effects fits and the banked-points state depend on a correct series grouping.
unreg:series_cumulative_points#u6.what_would_resolve: Pull a sample of playoff rows from leaguegamelog and Basketball-Reference and verify that series and game number can be reconstructed for every 2004-present playoff game.

unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.description: The catalog entry for this unregistered key is labelled as player/team counting specials (triple doubles, stat averages, one-off thresholds), while its only live series is now playoff single-game points; the playoff triple-double series in player_milestones uses the same union-over-playoff-games structure with separate inputs.
unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Relabel the archetype as playoff single-game player thresholds (or merge with KXNBAPLAYOFF3D) and replace its catalog input list with the inputs staged here.

unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.description: Opponent game plans that blitz or double a hot scorer, and a coach's willingness to play a star 45+ minutes, change the playoff 50-point tail, but neither is measured by any input.
unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Estimate from play-by-play the frequency of doubled possessions against stars by opponent coach and its effect on points per minute in playoff series.

unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.description: Overtime inclusion is not stated (KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE says 'including overtime' explicitly), and there is no rule for a player who is traded, suspended or ruled out for the playoffs before they begin; the record assumes official box-score points and No without a void.
unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Check settlements of KXNBAPLAYOFFPTS markets for injured players and the full rules text for an overtime clause.

unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.description: The text says 'any playoff game in the 2026 Pro Basketball Playoffs' without saying whether Play-In games count; other NBA series exclude the Play-In explicitly, which suggests they do not, but it is not stated here.
unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Request the full rules_secondary or check a settled KXNBAPLAYOFFPTS market for a player who scored highly in a Play-In game.

unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.description: Playoff 50-point games are rare (on the order of one per season league-wide in recent seasons, far fewer per player), so the playoff tail cannot be estimated directly; the record rescales a regular-season tail by playoff minutes and pace, and the size of that rescaling for the far tail is unverified.
unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials#.what_would_resolve: Fit the playoff-versus-regular-season tail ratio at 35+ and 40+ points over 20 seasons and test whether it extrapolates to 50.
